head: Code
Meaning
Reach for it when
rows: The pending affine transform applied to everything: value = base * mul + add
Many "apply to all" updates, lazy propagation
Adding to all values in O(1)
`mul *= m` and `add *= m`, because `(base*mul + add) * m`
Composing a multiplication into the transform
Stores `base = (val - add) / mul` so that `base * mul + add == val` today. Division is done with the modular inverse `pow(mul, MOD-2, MOD)`, valid as MOD is prime (Fermat's little theorem)
Adding a new item under an existing transform
`(vals[idx] * mul + add) % MOD`, or -1 if out of range

p: Calls from the example; `base` is what is stored in `vals`.

bullets: Time: O(1) for addAll, multAll and getIndex; O(log MOD) for append because of the modular inverse.

1622.takeaway: Store every value in a hidden form so that the real value is always stored * mul + add; then addAll and multAll only change two numbers.

head: Code
Meaning

rows: With one change, the pair can reach any sum from `min + 1` to `max + limit`
Range of sums reachable with one move
Starting cost 2 for every sum T (change both numbers)
Cost drops to 0 only at T = a + b
Prefix sums of `diff` turn the difference array into the actual total cost for each T

p: `nums = [1,2,4,3]`, `limit = 4`. The pairs are `(1,3)` with sum 4 (one move reaches sums 2 to 7) and `(2,4)` with sum 6 (one move reaches 3 to 8).

1674.takeaway: For every mirrored pair, count the cost of every target sum T with a difference array: 2 by default, 1 over a range, 0 at the pair's own sum; then take the best T.

head: Code
Meaning
Reach for it when
rows: For every subset of exactly `size` indices with all-distinct values, `max - min`
Precomputing the value of each possible group
Minimum total incompatibility to cover exactly the indices in `mask` with complete groups
Always build the group containing the lowest unused index
Avoids counting the same partition in many orders
The group contains `first` and does not reuse any used index
Bit tests for membership and disjointness
The full mask; `INF` means no valid split, so return -1

p: `nums = [1,2,1,4]`, `k = 2`, so groups have size 2. Valid pairs (distinct values): indices (0,1) cost 1, (0,3) cost 3, (1,2) cost 1, (1,3) cost 2, (2,3) cost 3. The pair (0,2) is invalid (two 1s).

bullets: Time: about O(2^n * S), where S is the number of valid groups (at most C(16, 8) = 12870).

1681.takeaway: Bitmask DP over the set of numbers already assigned: precompute the cost of every valid group, then add one group at a time that contains the lowest unused index.

p: `"aAa"` has no bad character, so it is returned. The top call picks the longer of `""` and `"aAa"`: `"aAa"`.

Space: O(n) recursion depth, plus the copied slices.

1763.takeaway: Divide and conquer: any letter missing its opposite case can never be in a nice substring, so split the string there and recurse on both sides.
